holidays.name: International Octopus Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the eight-armed, three-hearted, blue-blooded geniuses of the sea. Fans honor octopuses for their intelligence, camouflage skills, and talent for escaping aquarium tanks.
holidays.origin: The date, 10/8, was chosen as a pun on the octopus's eight arms (October is the 8th... well, 10 and 8 - 'Octo'). It is an unofficial observance promoted by ocean lovers and marine conservation fans.
holidays.funFact: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood, and two of its hearts stop beating when it swims, which is partly why it prefers crawling.

holidays.name: National Fluffernutter Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the sticky, sweet sandwich made with peanut butter and marshmallow creme on white bread. It is nostalgic comfort food at its gooiest.
holidays.origin: The Fluffernutter was popularized in New England in the early 20th century, after Durkee-Mower of Lynn, Massachusetts began marketing Marshmallow Fluff. The sandwich name came from a 1960s promotional campaign.
holidays.funFact: In 2006, a Massachusetts state senator proposed making a school-lunch limit on Fluffernutters, which sparked a 'Fluffernutter Rebellion' and a counter-bill to make it the official state sandwich.

holidays.name: National Pierogi Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy stuffed dumplings filled with potato, cheese, sauerkraut, meat, or even fruit. Pierogi fans mark the day by boiling, pan-frying, and topping them with sour cream and onions.
holidays.origin: Pierogi are rooted in Eastern European cuisine, especially Poland, and the day is an American food observance created to celebrate the beloved dumpling.
holidays.funFact: Pierogi are so popular in Cleveland, Ohio, and Whiting, Indiana, that both host festivals, and Cleveland's baseball stadium hosts pierogi races between costumed dumplings.

holidays.name: Free Thought Day
holidays.description: A day for questioning, reasoning, and celebrating independent thinking without dogma. It encourages people to explore ideas freely and thoughtfully.
holidays.origin: Observed in some secular and humanist circles, it grew out of freethought movements that began in earnest during the Enlightenment era and spread through 19th century societies.
holidays.funFact: The 'freethinker' label dates back to the late 1600s, when it was first used to describe people who formed opinions by reason rather than authority.

holidays.name: Underdog Day
holidays.description: A day to cheer for the long shots, the little guys, and anyone overlooked, from sports teams to cartoon dogs with capes. It encourages rooting for unlikely heroes.
holidays.origin: This unofficial observance is tied to the cartoon superhero dog 'Underdog,' who first aired in 1964 and made the phrase a pop culture staple.
holidays.funFact: Underdog, a humble shoeshine boy dog who fights villains in rhyming speech, was a balloon in the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade for years.
